edges.target: Aplasia or hypoplasia of the lacrimal glands

edges.description: Absent or hypoplastic lacrimal glands cannot supply the aqueous tear film.
Reduced aqueous tear production leaves the ocular surface dry and irritable.
Absent or hypoplastic major salivary glands reduce saliva production.
Distal obstruction of the drainage pathway lets the lacrimal sac distend.
Tears that cannot drain through atretic puncta or an obstructed duct overflow onto the face, so epiphora can coexist with reduced tear production.
Heterozygotes lack lacrimal gland primordia, as patients lack the gland.
edges.limitations: The mouse main lacrimal gland is exorbital with a long excretory duct, unlike the human intraorbital gland, and a small fraction of heterozygous primordia still show budding at E15.5.
Heterozygous mice show submandibular hypoplasia rather than the aplasia seen in many patients, and parotid development was not reported.
